summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with HCV- and alcohol-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and metastatic disease was admitted for altered mental status after taking extra Dilaudid. She was diagnosed with hepatic encephalopathy, likely triggered by constipation from opioids, and treated with increased lactulose and rifaximin, leading to improved mental status. She received Cyberknife radiation to a stable brain metastasis and completed three sessions for abdominal lymph node metastases. An MRI revealed a suspicious lesion at S1, possibly metastatic, contributing to chronic back pain. She had intermittent low-grade fevers without infection, managed with acetaminophen, and mild hyponatremia that resolved with fluids. Pre-syncopal episodes were attributed to volume shifts and deconditioning. Goals of care were reaffirmed as DNR/DNI, and she was discharged to extended care for rehabilitation with plans for outpatient follow-up and potential further radiation if back pain persisted.
